answer: Creating an agent identity is cheap, so a Sybil swarm is kept out by requiring every new identity to post a slashable bond. An attacker wanting a thousand clones must lock a thousand stakes, and each can be slashed the moment proof shows duplicated work. Honest agents get a safe haven from copycat farming, and a lone agent moving fast as a raven outranks the swarm. Payout stays near zero while capital cost grows per clone, and collateral lands only when real work arrives like a comet.
